categories.name: Central Storage
categories.description: The SpatialData .zarr the samples are added to.

categories.name: Sample Information
categories.description: What is added: Xenium or Atera bundles, or existing SpatialData objects (single- or multi-sample).

categories.name: Run params
categories.description: Optional CellTypist labels for every new sample.

parameters.name: Storage Location
parameters.description: A SpatialData .zarr (local path or s3://bucket/prefix) the samples are added to. If it doesn't exist, it is created at an s3:// prefix you can write to, or inside /results or /scratch.
parameters.help_text: A store you will keep adding to belongs on S3 (it is copied to /scratch, grown there and synced back). /results is a one-off build: saved as a data asset it is read-only. /scratch is cleared when the run ends. One run per store at a time.

parameters.name: Input type
parameters.description: Xenium and Atera bundles are read with their 10x readers; existing SpatialData objects are split into their samples. Every sample gets its own elements and table, and its cells join one joint single-cell table.
parameters.help_text: One type per run; run again with another type into the same store.

parameters.name: List of paths to samples
parameters.description: Bundle folders, bundle .zip files, SpatialData .zarr folders, folders holding them, or globs, separated by commas. EX: /data/xenium_runs, /data/extra/sample_outs.zip
parameters.help_text: A folder holding experiment.xenium (Xenium) or experiment.spatial (Atera) is one sample; any other folder's direct children are the samples. Sample IDs come from the folder or .zip name (without _outs), or a SpatialData's sample_id column. Samples already in the store are skipped.

parameters.name: Custom Celltypist model (.pkl, optional)
parameters.description: A CellTypist model trained for your gene panel; its labels are added to every new sample. Empty = no labels. EX: /data/models/my_panel_model.pkl
parameters.help_text: The file name (without .pkl) names the label columns, and a store keeps the model it was built with, so use the same file for every run into one store.
